newsitem.title: UK: UK IMRO fines Invesco for breaking rules.
newsitem.headline: UK IMRO fines Invesco for breaking rules.

text.p: British investments watchdog IMRO said on Thursday it had fined Invesco Asset Management 60,000 pounds ($97,400) for breaches of its rules on client money.

The Investment Management Regulatory Organisation said in a statement Invesco, which is now part of investment management group Amvesco Plc, would also have to pay costs of 25,000 pounds, after agreeing to settle disciplinary proceedings against it.

IMRO said Invesco, which merged with AIM Management Group Inc, had failed to reconcile client money bank accounts on time, failed to correct differences on reconciliations and failed to maintain written compliance procedures.

This is the third time that Invesco has fallen foul of the watchdog. In 1991, Invesco MIM Management was fined 75,000 pounds for failings in dealing with Personal Equity Plan (PEP) administration and client money, affecting 110,000 people and 220 million pounds of investments.

This investigation led to a much larger 750,000 pounds fine and over 1.5 million pounds of costs in June 1993, when Invesco MIM, Invesco MIM Unit Trust Managers and Invesco Ventures faced 55 charges relating to widespread management and procedural failings.
Invesco Asset management has around 5.5 billion pounds under management for institutional and retail customers, including around 80,000 PEP investors.
